item.title: Lassana Cissé murder trial: accused breaks down in tears as crime-scene photos shown
item.description: Lorin Scicluna, charged with the 2019 murder of Lassana Cissé in Birżebbuġa and three counts of attempted murder, broke down and was briefly escorted out of the courtroom on Wednesday as jurors were shown 59 graphic photographs from the crime scene, including autopsy close-ups and bullet-entry wounds. The day also featured 112-call recordings from taxi driver Christopher Bernard Farrugia, who first reported Cissés body, and testimony from emergency nurse Patrick Bonnett and scene-of-crime officers Michelle Camilleri and Mario Azzopardi.
item.content:encoded:
Lorin Scicluna, charged with the 2019 murder of Lassana Cissé in Birżebbuġa and three counts of attempted murder, broke down and was briefly escorted out of the courtroom on Wednesday as jurors were shown 59 graphic photographs from the crime scene, including autopsy close-ups and bullet-entry wounds. The day also featured 112-call recordings from taxi driver Christopher Bernard Farrugia, who first reported Cissés body, and testimony from emergency nurse Patrick Bonnett and scene-of-crime officers Michelle Camilleri and Mario Azzopardi.

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: Q2 government deficit down €35.2m after accounting adjustment
item.description: Maltas consolidated government deficit stood at €344.1million in the second quarter of 2026, the NSO said on Wednesday €35.2million lower than the cash-based figure after the Consolidated Fund was restated under ESA2010 accrual accounting. Government revenue rose €212.3million year-on-year, led by income/wealth tax (+€141.2m), while expenditure climbed €321.5m on higher intermediate consumption and salaries; government debt reached €11.98billion or 47.0% of GDP at the end of June.

item.title: Aquilina names ex-police sergeant as kingpin behind AI smear campaign
item.description: Former Repubblika head Robert Aquilina on Wednesday said retired sergeant Joseph Abela father of a serving inspector and brother of retired judge Toni Abela was behind an AI-generated image that portrayed him as Lord of the Rings Gollum, part of a wider dehumanisation campaign against government critics. Aquilina said he has reported Abela to police and asked for a separate inquiry into claims of suppression; Repubblika backed him and urged police to act without fear or favour.

item.title: Bedingfield backs prisons chief after mobile-phone breach
item.description: Home affairs minister Glenn Bedingfield on Wednesday reiterated confidence in prisons director Christopher Siegersma after three inmates George Degiorgio, Robert Agius and Damiano Torrisi were found with mobile phones in their cells over the weekend, with two suspected of using them to plot a murder. The minister announced a new internal professional-standards unit and a draft law that would make using or smuggling a phone into prison a criminal offence rather than a disciplinary breach.

item.title: Malta must shift from workforce growth to productivity, Chamber president warns
item.description: Malta Chamber president William Spiteri Bailey told the EY Future Realised Conference on Wednesday that Maltas economic growth has been propped up by an expanding workforce rather than productivity, and warned that infrastructure, education and skills gaps risk undermining the countrys attractiveness. He pointed to investor satisfaction with transport infrastructure falling to 14%, 69% of investors unable to find specialised skills locally, and PISA 2025 scores dropping by 1331 points across science, maths and reading.

item.title: Fish-farm fines must make operators think twice, EU fisheries chief says
item.description: EU Commissioner for Fisheries Costas Kads, on a visit to Malta, said penalties for aquaculture operators should act as a real deterrent given the value of the industry, after four tuna farms were collectively fined just 14,000 in 2025 over fish-farm slime on the eastern coast. He promised continued EU support for Maltese fishermen facing Tunisian competition, citing 25 suspected infringements detected this season via a drone operation, and warned that climate change and invasive species are reshaping Mediterranean fisheries.

item.title: Bolt failure probably contributed to Swiss climbers fatal Zurrieq fall
item.description: ClimbMT said on Wednesday that a failure of a 316-stainless belay bolt at the first belay of the Plunder route at Wied Fulija, Zurrieq most probably caused the October11 fall that killed 55-year-old Swiss climber Daniel Fransson. The federation has alerted the UIAA and will prioritise inspections on coastal crags, urging climbers never to rely on a single bolt as their only protection.

item.title: Sicily strike: PN says empty shelves expose need for more local production
item.description: The Nationalist Party said on Wednesday that supermarket shelves emptied by the Sicilian truckers fuel-price strike prove Malta must produce more of its own food, calling on the government to give farmers, livestock breeders, self-employed workers and small businesses more tools to compete. Shadow agriculture minister Toni Bezzina and shadow small-enterprise minister Michael Piccinino warned that local production is a matter of national security and peace of mind for Maltese and Gozitan families.

item.title: Renewables now 18.8% of Maltas energy consumption, Eurostat data shows
item.description: Maltas renewable-energy share rose 1.6 percentage points to 18.8% of final energy consumption in 2025, provisional Eurostat data cited by the Energy Ministry on Wednesday showed, leaving it ahead of Belgium, Slovakia and Ireland. Energy minister Miriam Dalli said the trend underlines the value of sustained investment and the role of households and businesses in making renewable energy more accessible and affordable while strengthening energy security.

item.title: Malta climbs rule of law rankings to 29th despite drop in key freedoms
item.description: Malta climbed two places to 29th out of 143 countries in the World Justice Projects 2026 Rule of Law Index, despite a less-than-one-per-cent drop in its overall score to 0.67. The report flagged declines in freedom of expression, freedom of assembly and public participation, with Maltas ranking on constraints on government powers sliding to 49th this year from 39th in 2024, and noted government powers limited by the judiciary fell in 63 per cent of countries, including Malta. Malta rose two places to 38th globally for absence of corruption and ranked 10th for order and security, retaining 7th in the EU/North America region.

item.title: Hungry crocodiles threaten EU climate goals, PM Abela warns
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela on Wednesday likened the EUs 2050 climate-neutrality ambition to a castle surrounded by hungry crocodiles, insisting that protecting households from rising energy costs is compatible with the clean-energy transition. Speaking at the EY attractiveness-survey conference, he acknowledged subsidies prolong dependence on fossil fuels but rejected the idea that consumer protection and decarbonisation are mutually exclusive, projecting a 2.2% GDP contraction if subsidies were removed. A third Sicily interconnector will be operational by end of Q1 2027, he said; opposition leader Alex Borg welcomed investor-confidence figures but warned they do not measure investment actually delivered.

item.title: €1.5m CPD headquarters enlargement unveiled with AI-equipped control room
item.description: Home affairs minister Glenn Bedingfield on Wednesday unveiled a 1.5million renovation of the Civil Protection Department headquarters that doubles its size and upgrades its emergency-response control room with state-of-the-art equipment. Fire engines are now fitted with cameras allowing officials to track operations in real time, with an AI-assisted system able to transmit data and, if needed, be extended to another three or four rooms. CPD director general Peter Paul Coleiro said the expanded premises match the departments wider remit since the original 1990s build.

item.title: Government unveils seven-point, 1m plan to tackle Oriental hornets
item.description: The government on Wednesday announced a 1million, seven-point plan to tackle a surge in Oriental hornets and support the beekeeping sector, after beekeepers warned throughout the summer that hornets were devastating their colonies. The plan covers a research programme into hornet-control technologies, a new-colony support scheme that prioritises the native Maltese honey bee (Apis mellifera ruttneri), per-colony financial aid for losses during 2026, conservation breeding, a national nest-reporting hotline and a public-awareness campaign. Implementation begins immediately, the Agriculture Ministry said.

item.title: Prosecution Lays Out Case in Scicluna Murder Trial: 'There's a Body on the Street'
item.description: On day two of Lorin Scicluna's jury trial for the 2019 racially-motivated murder of Lassana Cisse, prosecutors played 112 emergency calls and walked jurors through the night the 42-year-old Ivorian father of two was shot dead on a dark road between Birżebbuġa and Ħal Far. Two police witnesses described arriving at Triq il-Ġebel to find victims Mohammed Jallow shot in the penis and Ibrahim Bah wounded in the backside. Defence cross-examination began Tuesday. Scicluna, 29, a former AFM soldier, has pleaded not guilty to nine charges including murder, attempted murder and a February 2019 hit-and-run that injured May Malimi. He faces up to life imprisonment if convicted.

item.title: Unions Warn of 'Hidden Agendas' Threatening KM Malta Airlines After Minister's Remarks
item.description: Four trade unions representing KM Malta Airlines workers — the GWU, Union of Cabin Crew, Airline Pilots Association Malta, and Association of Airline Engineers Malta — have publicly expressed concern over Finance Minister Clyde Caruana's recent warnings of "hidden agendas" and "undercurrents" trying to derail the national carrier. The unions said such comments risk creating uncertainty for employees whose livelihoods depend on the airline, and insisted that "the future of KM Malta Airlines is a matter of national importance and should be approached with responsibility, transparency and mutual respect." They rejected any narrative that treats legitimate worker concerns as suspicious.

item.title: Audit Finds Government Board Members Paid Despite Holding No Meetings
item.description: The National Audit Office found that "in a few cases" board members on government-appointed bodies received their annual remuneration during 2023 even though no formal meetings were convened that year. The audit covered 462 bodies and 3,901 members, with around €9 million paid out in total; just over €500,000 of that could not be fully verified. Auditors also flagged incorrect board categorisations that overstated pay, and a handful of ministries that failed to submit documentation.

item.title: Government to Spend €400 Million on Energy and Fuel Subsidies in 2026 — and Another €400 Million in 2027
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana told parliament that government expects to spend around €400 million on energy and fuel subsidies in 2026 — more than double the €172 million allocated in the previous budget — with a similar €400 million projected for 2027. Replying to a parliamentary question from Labour MP Alex Muscat, Caruana said international fuel price pressures are driving the increase and that there is currently no projected end date for the subsidies. He rejected calls from the Malta Chamber to begin phasing the support out, arguing that Malta's fiscal position is "completely different" from countries where recent protests have erupted.

item.title: Revolut Hit by Service Disruption Affecting Users in Malta and Across Europe
item.description: Revolut users in Malta and several other European countries lost access to parts of the fintech platform Tuesday morning, with all 30 services — including card payments, transfers and currency exchange — marked "partially unavailable" on the company's status page. The outage came as Google separately reported "multiple" Cloud services network failures across Europe. Revolut said its engineering team was "actively working to restore full service as quickly as possible." The disruption affected customers in Spain, Ireland, Germany, Italy and the UK, according to social media reports.

item.title: Magħtab Landfill to Be Dug Deeper for 2.9 Million Cubic Metres of Extra Waste Capacity
item.description: WasteServ has issued a tender to deepen the existing engineered Magħtab landfill from 10 to 54 metres — adding more than 2.9 million cubic metres of capacity, equivalent to 1,100 Olympic-sized swimming pools — without taking any additional land. The project will be carried out in two phases; excavated bedrock will be processed into construction products to offset costs, and waste removed ahead of excavation will be repurposed. WasteServ CEO Richard Bilocca said the goal is to make the best possible use of existing infrastructure while Malta works to reduce reliance on landfilling.

item.title: Court Expert: 'White Powder' in Mosta Drug Raid Was Cocaine and Washing Powder
item.description: Two men accused of trafficking more than a kilo of cocaine were actually in possession of 125 grams of the drug, while other white powder seized at their Mosta residences was probably washing powder, court chemist Gilbert Mercieca testified Tuesday. The substances were found alongside jewellery and mobile phones during a police investigation that led to June charges against Justin Chetcuti, 33, and Jean Paul Spiter, 31. Both have pleaded not guilty and are out on bail.

item.title: Gozo Ferry Passenger Numbers Drop on Mġarr–Ċirkewwa and Mġarr–Valletta, Buġibba Service Picks Up
item.description: Passenger numbers on the main Mġarr–Ċirkewwa ferry fell 3.3% in the third quarter of this year compared with the same period in 2025, the National Statistics Office said Tuesday, while the Mġarr–Valletta fast ferry saw a steeper 9.1% drop in passengers despite running 5.8% more trips. The picture was brighter for the newer Buġibba and Sliema services launched in May: together they carried roughly 143,000 passengers in the quarter, with passenger volumes growing across all four legs from July through September. Total Gozo ferry trips reached 14,417 for the quarter, carrying 2,141,312 passengers.

item.title: Police Ordered John Cassar to Report Hours Before His Mother's Murder, Court Hears
item.description: Police ordered John Cassar, 47, to report for questioning over a domestic violence complaint filed by his estranged wife just hours before he allegedly murdered his mother and tried to kill his father in Mqabba last week. Cassar appeared before Magistrate Kevan Azzopardi on Tuesday facing fresh charges of allegedly harassing his wife online and of breaking a protection order, saying he was not aware his parents were still alive. Magistrates heard he sent messages and published Facebook posts about his wife on October 13 and 14; a risk assessment found she was not at immediate risk of life and the case was listed as inconclusive.

item.title: Second €35 Million Reverse Osmosis Plant Being Built at Għar Lapsi
item.description: A new €35 million reverse osmosis plant is being built at Għar Lapsi alongside Malta's oldest, with six systems producing 30,000 cubic metres of potable water a day. The existing plant stays fully operational throughout. The project forms part of the Water Services Corporation's National Investment Plan, which will invest more than €400 million in Maltese water infrastructure over the coming decade.

item.title: Labour Plans Two-Year Drive to Ask 350,000 Voters Three Questions
item.description: The Labour Party will run a two-year outreach programme dubbed 'Listening to Malta and Gozo' aimed at drawing feedback from 350,000 voters nationwide, party CEO Ivan Falzon said. Volunteers will knock on doors, make calls, run open discussion events and drive responses through online forms and a mobile app. Respondents will be asked what they would like to improve, what they would like to preserve, and what they would like the party to understand.

item.description: Statistics presented in parliament show 1,778 domestic violence cases involving 1,910 victims were registered in Malta and Gozo between 1 January and 14 October 2026. Some 1,245 victims were women and 665 men, with 127 children under 18 and 257 people aged 60 or over among them. Malta recorded 1,638 cases and Gozo 140.

item.title: PN Calls for Review of School Bus Routes Over 90-Minute Journeys
item.description: The Nationalist Party called for an urgent revision of school transport routes and an increase in capacity after parents reported children waking at 5.15am and facing more than 90 minutes of travel each way. The party said the journeys eat into children's rest, study and family time, and that free school transport must be efficient enough to stop parents defaulting to their own cars. It wants a review in consultation with parents, schools and operators.

item.title: Unions Warn of 'Hidden Agendas' Threatening KM Malta Airlines
item.description: Four trade unions representing KM Malta Airlines workers — the GWU, Union of Cabin Crew, Airline Pilots Association Malta, and Association of Airline Engineers Malta — have expressed concern over Finance Minister Clyde Caruana's warnings of "hidden agendas" trying to derail the national carrier. The unions said such comments risk creating uncertainty for employees and insisted the airline's future is a matter of national importance that should be approached with responsibility, transparency and mutual respect.

item.title: Government to Spend €400 Million on Energy and Fuel Subsidies in 2026
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana told parliament the government expects to spend around €400 million on energy and fuel subsidies in 2026 — more than double the €172 million in the previous budget — with a similar €400 million projected for 2027. International fuel price pressures are driving the increase and there is no projected end date for the subsidies. Caruana rejected calls from the Malta Chamber to begin phasing the support out.

item.title: Magħtab Landfill to Be Dug Deeper for 2.9 Million Cubic Metres Extra Capacity
item.description: WasteServ has issued a tender to deepen the existing engineered Magħtab landfill from 10 to 54 metres — adding more than 2.9 million cubic metres of capacity without taking any additional land. The project will run in two phases; excavated bedrock will be processed into construction products to offset costs. CEO Richard Bilocca said the goal is to make the best use of existing infrastructure while Malta works to reduce reliance on landfilling.

item.title: Gozo Ferry Passenger Numbers Drop on Main Routes, Buġibba Service Picks Up
item.description: Passenger numbers on the main Mġarr–Ċirkewwa ferry fell 3.3% in the third quarter compared with the same period in 2025, the National Statistics Office said, while the Mġarr–Valletta fast ferry saw a steeper 9.1% drop despite running 5.8% more trips. The newer Buġibba and Sliema services launched in May carried roughly 143,000 passengers between them. Total Gozo ferry trips reached 14,417 for the quarter, carrying 2,141,312 passengers.

item.title: Government opens two new electricity distribution centres, upgrades Msida
item.description: The government inaugurated distribution centres in Naxxar and Siġġiewi on Wednesday and announced the upgrading of the Msida centre, together serving some 33,000 households and businesses across 11 localities. The Naxxar centre will feed Naxxar, Għargħur and Burmarrad while easing pressure on Mosta, and the Siġġiewi centre comes with 70km of new medium-voltage cable to strengthen supply for around 12,000 consumers in Siġġiewi, Mqabba, Qrendi, Żebbuġ and Qormi. Works in Msida doubled capacity from 30 MVA to 60 MVA, improving reliability for Mater Dei Hospital and the University of Malta. Malta now has 23 distribution centres.

item.title: BCA seals off uninhabitable Paceville block after owners ignore warnings
item.description: The Building and Construction Authority has begun emergency works on the evacuated Seaview Apartments in Paceville, saying owners must pay after ignoring repeated warnings. Concrete blocks were placed around the former Burger King entrance and a temporary shield is being built to stabilise the building and seal off access. Residents were evacuated in August after the block was declared no longer fit for habitation, following a long-running dispute among owners over who should carry out maintenance.

item.title: Lorin Scicluna murder trial enters fourth day with further witnesses due to testify
item.description: The trial of former soldier Lorin Scicluna resumed on Thursday morning at the Valletta law courts, with prosecutors expected to call further witnesses in the case over the racially motivated murder of Lassana Cisse. Scicluna, 46, faces nine charges including the murder of Cisse and the attempted murder of Mohammed Jallow, Ibrahim Bah and May Malimi, and could face life imprisonment if convicted. He denies all charges. Jurors were shown on Wednesday graphic photographs of Cisse’s body, and the trial is being presided over by Judge Natasha Galea Sciberras.

item.title: Planning Authority defers 13-storey Palazzina Vincenti hotel conversion amid heritage campaign
item.description: The Planning Authority deferred a decision on developer Carlo Stivali’s application (PA/07761/21) to turn the Grade 2 listed postwar modernist Palazzina Vincenti in St Julian’s into a 13-storey hotel, citing a lack of consent and contracts with neighbouring owners. Kamra tal-Periti, the Flimkien għal-Ambjent Aħjar NGO, St Julian’s residents and the KTP have all called for the building’s protection to be upgraded to Grade 1 or for it to be expropriated for public use. Architect Gustavo R Vincenti designed the St Julian’s property as his own home in 1952, and a 2021 Superintendence of Cultural Heritage report described it as one of the best modernist examples in Malta.

item.title: Swedish socialist MEP accuses EPP of exploiting Daphne murder in rule of law clash
item.description: A Swedish socialist MEP accused the European People Party, which Malta’s PN MEPs sit within, of exploiting the murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia for political gain, and questioned whether the European Parliament had become a "Mickey Mouse parliament". The intervention came as Malta’s two MEPs traded blows in the Strasbourg plenary debate on the rule of law, held to mark nine years since Caruana Galizia’s assassination. Prime Minister Robert Abela separately criticised PN MEPs over their stance.

item.title: Daphne Caruana Galizia journalism prize awarded in Strasbourg as her family attends
item.description: Caruana Galizia’s family attended the presentation in Strasbourg of the European Parliament’s Daphne Caruana Galizia prize for journalism, awarded to Giacomo Zandonini and Maite Vermeulen for an 18-month investigation into Italy’s migrant detention deal with Albania. The reporters, published by De Correspondent, filed over 30 freedom of information requests across six European countries and to the Commission, the Council and Frontex, and were denied access to the Italian-run facilities. The award was presented during the same sitting at which Malta’s rule of law was debated.

item.title: Labour MEPs welcome €3.7m in EU funds for Storm Harry damage
item.description: Labour MEPs Alex Agius Saliba, Daniel Attard and Thomas Bajada welcomed the allocation of €3.7 million in EU funds to Malta following the damage caused by Storm Harry in January. Malta had calculated the storm’s total cost at around €128 million, with extensive harm to public infrastructure, homes, businesses and livelihoods across Malta and Gozo. The MEPs described the assistance as a concrete demonstration of European solidarity in the recovery effort.

item.title: Malta’s investor attractiveness climbs to 81%, EY survey shows
item.description: Malta’s attractiveness as a destination for foreign direct investment has risen for a second consecutive year, with 81% of surveyed investors viewing the country positively, according to EY’s Malta Attractiveness Survey. That is up from 79% in 2025 and 54% in 2024, and the highest rating recorded since 2016, when it stood at 87%. Only 13% of respondents now consider Malta unattractive, down from 25% two years ago. Investor sentiment had bottomed out at 37% in 2021.

item.title: Maltese rank joint second in world for daily worry, Gallup report finds
item.description: Maltese adults are among the world’s biggest worriers, with 58% saying they worried "a lot" on the previous day, placing Malta joint second out of 140 countries and territories in Gallup’s 2025 State of the World’s Emotional Health report. The figure compares with a global average of 38%, behind only the Republic of the Congo at 60%. Malta nonetheless scored above global averages on feeling respected (93% against 83%), smiling or laughing (77% against 72%) and feeling well-rested (76% against 71%).

item.title: Cerviola Hotel in Marsascala to be demolished and replaced with eight-storey, 99-room complex
item.description: Cerviola Holidays Ltd has applied to the Planning Authority to demolish the existing 50-room Cerviola Hotel in Triq il-Qaliet, Marsascala, and replace it with an eight-storey, 99-room four-star hotel. The application (PA/07388/26), drawn up by architect Edwin Mintoff, would add two swimming pools, a spa, gym, restaurant, rooftop bar and a 101-square-metre multipurpose hall. The ground floor would hold a restaurant of about 188 square metres, and 93 of the 99 rooms would be twins.

item.title: Abela declines to guarantee Nigret and Żebbuġ services will avoid government land
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela refused to say whether government land in the Nigret area would be used for the roads, mains, electrical cables and drainage infrastructure needed to serve a block of private apartments in Żurrieq that is being approved. Asked directly whether the policy of no private development on government land also covers such public works, Abela pointed instead to the 2006 rationalisation process and repeated that he had been very clear on the policy, without addressing the question directly.

item.title: Gozo records the most community police patrol hours in Malta
item.description: Gozo leads the localities with the highest number of community police patrol hours, according to a table presented in parliament by Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield covering January to September 2026. Gozo recorded 6,529 patrol hours and 189.4km covered on bicycle, followed by Rabat Malta/Imdina/Ħad-Dingli/Imtarfa with 4,568.4 hours and Marsaxlokk/Birżebbuġa with 4,207.65 hours. Ħaż-Żebbuġ and Siġġiewi covered the most kilometres on patrol. The figures came in response to a question by Nationalist MP Bernice Bonello.

item.title: Clocks go back an hour at 3am on Sunday
item.description: Summer time in Malta ends at 3am on Sunday 25 October, when clocks go back by one hour, leaving the country on UTC+1. All EU states currently switch to winter time on the last Sunday of October. Most phones, tablets and laptops will adjust automatically, but clocks elsewhere will need to be reset manually.

item.title: Hornets may pose a danger to Malta’s stray cats, parliamentary secretary says
item.description: Parliamentary Secretary Alicia Bugeja Said has met the Malta Beekeepers Association to discuss the oriental hornet population in Malta and the risk the insects pose to stray cats as well as bees. The discussions covered how cat feeders and volunteers could be supported in reducing conditions that attract hornets to areas where stray animals are fed. Bugeja Said said further meetings would be held to identify practical solutions.

item.title: Shooting survivors mistook gunfire for fireworks, Cisse murder jury hears
item.description: The trial of former soldier Lorin Scicluna entered its fourth day, with testimonies read out from survivors Mohammed Jallow and Ibrahim Bah, who initially believed the shooting that killed Lassana Cisse in April 2019 was fireworks. Scicluna denies attempting to murder them in a racially motivated attack and faces up to life imprisonment; the court heard phone records and mobile antenna activity from the night of the killing. Judge Natasha Galea Sciberras is presiding.
